prompt: The evaluation repository asks the agent to "design a blinded LLM benchmark". The evidence packet contains missingness, duplicates, unit ambiguity, and an attractive aggregate that can change the unit of analysis. The acceptance boundary is ml-evaluation: Define deployment tasks, populations, failures, costs, baselines, and thresholds before metrics. The adjacent analytics-engineering discipline is a routing decoy unless its separate responsibility is actually requested. Resolve environment facts that change the answer, preserve existing contracts and user-owned state, and produce reproducible success plus failure or recovery evidence. A happy path alone is insufficient.

requirements: timestamped transactions with repeated account identities, class imbalance and a planted train/test near-duplicate leakage path
raw preprocessing/feature-selection pipeline plus current and candidate probabilistic classifiers
development and final temporal periods, review-capacity/error-cost contract and baseline predictions
per-example probabilities plus account/time/source slices and injected invalid/missing-label rows
representative negative, interruption, compatibility, or recovery path

falsifiableChecks.assertion: The result must establish the actual ml-evaluation boundary and relevant environment before acting, preserve the hierarchy relationship (broader=data-analysis,testing-engineering; children=computer-vision,embedding-systems,fine-tuning-training,llm-evaluation,recommendation-ranking,speech-audio-ai; near-neighbor=analytics-engineering), and not absorb the near-neighbor responsibility merely because it is adjacent.
Define deployment tasks, populations, failures, costs, baselines, and thresholds before metrics.
The result must make its consequential assumptions, ownership, and decision sequence explicit and reproducible.
Evaluation protocol; Baseline and slices; Failure analysis
The result must not treat a happy path, generated artifact, compilation, or unsupported assumption as sufficient proof of ml-evaluation correctness.

Every material completion claim must map to observable evidence (Deployment target/population, loss or failure-cost contract and current/dummy baseline; Leakage-safe train/development/test split identity plus preprocessing/model/calibration/threshold versions; Per-example paired predictions with decision-aligned metrics, calibration/threshold evidence and uncertainty; Predeclared slice, temporal/drift, invalid-row and regression evidence), with simulated, unavailable, inferred, stale, or unresolved evidence labeled rather than converted into certainty.
